rules: Figma is the visual source of truth. Every template links to its Figma frames. Those designs are meant to be built as designed, not reinterpreted. Fonts, colors, sizes and positions come from Figma. If something in Figma can't be built or looks inconsistent, raise it, don't silently change it.

This spec is for auto-generation first. Everything here describes how the app generates postcards automatically (the Flow 1/2 output set and "Generate another"). Manual postcard creation (Flow 3) is not fully specified yet. Where a template has notes on manual mode, they're preliminary and marked as such.
Only build templates marked ready-for-dev. Other statuses are shown for context and planning.

Never invent data. When a field is missing, follow the template's fallback rules. If a fallback isn't defined, the template isn't eligible for auto-generation in that case. This follows Core Engine FR-1: missing values are explicit unknowns, never guessed.

Every text field declares its source. Each one is either generated by AI (and at which engine stage), filled by software from existing data, or static. This matches the template catalog that Core Engine Stage 3 expects (Core Engine PRD 4.8, 5.5 and prompt 9.8).

AI text constraints are guidance, not hard limits. Character limits are written into the AI prompts so the output fits naturally. The software limits (shrinking text, trimming) are only a safety net for extreme cases.
templates.json wins. If the website and the JSON ever disagree, the JSON is correct. Every change bumps the version and adds a changelog line.
readyForDevChecklist: Figma section named with the tracker number; frames and layers use clear names (photo_slot, line_1, message...)
Output sizes confirmed; unused frames removed
Text blocks built with auto-layout or fixed text boxes, so they adapt to the length of the text
Every field has a source, constraints and a fallback
No open blockers (asset swaps that don't change the layout can be followUps)

stage1.place.locality.what: City, town or place from GPS (a stored explicit unknown if missing)

stage1b.sticker_text.line_1.what: New AI field, per photo (see template #1)

stage1b.sticker_text.line_2.what: New AI field, per photo (see template #1)

static.what: Fixed text or asset in the design

templates.name: 3-line text sticker
templates.summary: A three-line text sticker over a full-bleed photo. Line 1 is one bold uppercase word, line 2 continues the description in lowercase script, and line 3 is the place. Example: "OUTDOOR / summer festival / south bank of the Tagus". Because its text is generated for every photo in Stage 1b, it's available for any image in the app that has the data.

layers.name: photo_slot
layers.what: The photo, full bleed, cover crop

layers.name: photo_dim (black 30%)
layers.what: Black overlay at 30% over the photo, for legibility. Part of the template.

layers.name: bg_base
layers.what: Base fill behind the photo (not visible when a photo is present)

layers.name: sticker_text
layers.what: Vertical auto-layout block holding the 3 lines (spacing 0, left aligned)

photos.crop: Full bleed, cover-cropped to the output size.
photos.groupSelection: n/a, applies to any single photo with the required data.

fields.label: Line 1
fields.constraints: One word, ideally 5-12 characters. If the leading word is under 5 characters, use it plus the next word, as long as together they stay within 12.
fields.aiGuidance: sticker_text: a short caption of what the photo shows, split across two lines of a sticker. line_1: the leading word of the caption, ideally 5 to 12 letters (for example "Outdoor"). If the most natural leading word is shorter than 5 letters, you may use two words, as long as together they stay within 12 letters. Together, line_1 + line_2 must read as one natural phrase. Aim for the sweet spot between sounding natural and fitting these lengths. Treat the lengths as targets, not hard rules. Describe only what is visible. No feelings, no identities or relationships, and no place names (the place is added separately). Follows Core Engine Section 8 guardrails.
fields.safetyNet: Software shrink: render at max size, reduce down to min size if too wide. Below min size: if two words, keep only the first word; a single word may go below minimum.

fields.label: Line 2
fields.constraints: Continues line 1 as one natural phrase. About 20 characters.
fields.aiGuidance: line_2: the rest of the caption, about 20 characters or fewer (for example "summer festival"). Treat the length as a target, not a hard rule.
fields.safetyNet: Software shrink down to min size. Below min size: wrap onto a second line. Never rewrite or cut words.
fields.fallback: of my travel (or of my trip, see fallback cases)

fields.label: Line 3
fields.safetyNet: Software shrink down to min size. Below min size: use the country instead (or "in {country}" in the place-only case).
fields.fallback: Country, see fallback cases for the rest.

autoGeneration.eligibleWhen: line_1 and line_2 exist and a place (locality or country) exists. This is the priority case.
autoGeneration.priority: High: eligible for almost any photo with the required data.
notes: The partial and empty fallback cases are for when the user picks this template themselves. They're not auto-generated.
Max 1 per output set (the 3-7 postcard set), because the sticker qualifies for almost every photo and would crowd out other templates.
Applies to any photo, including photos tagged out in Stage 1 (they still have Stage 1b output). Auto-generation only uses grouped photos, through Stage 3 matching.
In Stage 3's template catalog, line_1 and line_2 are marked precomputed per photo, so Stage 3 must not rewrite them. line_3 is marked software-filled.

fallbackCases.then: line_1 and line_2 generated; line_3 = locality, else country
line_1 and line_2 generated; line_3 dropped
line_1 = A PIECE; line_2 = of my trip; line_3 = in {place}, {country}
line_1 = A PIECE; line_2 = of my travel; line_3 = memories

fallbackCases.when: Place and country are the same (Singapore, Monaco) or there's no locality
"in {place}, {country}" doesn't fit at line 3's minimum size

rendering: Color: fixed yellow #F2C305 on all three lines for the MVP.
Shadow: on the whole text block, drop shadow, black 35%, offset x 0 y 2, blur 12, spread 0.
Layout: the three lines stack with 0 spacing, left aligned. The block sits 48px from the left edge and is vertically centered in the frame. Line 3 is indented 84px.
Safe width: 48px side margins, so each line's width (including line 3's indent) must fit within 984px.
Shrink rule (all lines): render at max size; if a line is wider than the safe width, reduce its font size until it fits, down to its min size. In the Figma example, line 3 is already shrunk to 78px.

Below min size (extreme cases only): line_1 drops to one word if two words still don't fit (a single word may go below minimum); line_2 wraps onto a second line, never rewritten or cut; line_3 uses the country instead.
Fonts Kaisei Tokumin and Imperial Script are Google Fonts; bundle them in the app.

notes: The user can apply this sticker to any photo. The text is prefilled from the data, or from the fallbacks above, and can be edited. Editing limits and placement are to be revisited before manual mode is specified.

engineDependencies.change: Add sticker_text (line_1, line_2) as a new per-photo AI field in Stage 1b. Burst frames and near-duplicates inherit it like the other AI fields (FR-3).
engineDependencies.specRef: Core Engine 5.2 (AI fields), 4.3 (prompt and schema changes), Stage 1b prompt in Section 9, FR-3

templates.name: Vintage postcard
templates.summary: A vintage postcard: the photo sits in a framed slot at the top, and the postcard back sits below it, with a stamp and ruled message lines. The message is generated from the photo's place and year. This postcard works best for photos that are wider than they are tall.

layers.name: card_art (frame, back, lines)
layers.what: One image holding the photo frame, the postcard back, the divider and the ruled lines

layers.name: old_stamp_cover (card paper patch)
layers.what: A patch of the card's own paper that hides the old stamp baked into card_art. Export it together with card_art, or re-export card_art flattened with the patch.

layers.name: stamp
layers.what: The "MEMORY" suitcase stamp (PNG with transparent perforated edges), 160x165, at x 808 y 845 in the 2:3 frame and x 812 y 1037 in the 9:16 frame. Subtle shadow: black 18%, y 2, blur 4.

photos.crop: Fixed landscape slot of 859x546 (about 3:2) that exactly fills the window inside the cream photo frame. The photo must stay inside the frame's border, never overlap it. Position: x 107, y 215 in the 2:3 frame; x 110.75, y 407 in the 9:16 frame. Cover crop into the slot (fill the slot, center, crop the overflow). A portrait photo gets a center crop.
photos.groupSelection: In a group: use the group cover (stage2.group.cover_photo) if it's landscape. Otherwise use the group's landscape photo with the highest appeal score (stage1b.appeal_score); if there's none, center-crop the cover.

fields.label: Message
fields.constraints: Pattern "A snapshot of {place}, {country}. {year}". Wraps across the ruled lines, max 4 lines.
fields.safetyNet: Shrink rule: if the message needs more than 4 lines at 42px, reduce the font size, down to a minimum of 34px. If it still doesn't fit, use the shorter fallback.

render.lineHeight: 64px (locked to the ruled lines, never changes when shrinking)

autoGeneration.eligibleWhen: The photo has at least a country. Landscape photos are strongly preferred.
autoGeneration.priority: No AI text: everything is filled by software, so in the Stage 3 catalog the AI only decides whether the template fits the group.
notes: The year is the capture year of the photo used, not the trip's.
"Wish you were here." appears only when there's no location data. In every other case the generated message replaces it.
A version using the traveler's own input (human data) is out of scope for now.

fallbackCases.when: Place and country both available and different
Message doesn't fit in 4 lines at minimum size

rendering: Message font: Jacques Francois Regular (Google Font), 42px, left aligned, black.
Line height: 64px, locked to the ruled lines. Never change the line height when shrinking, so the text always sits on the lines.

Message box: fixed width 393px, height grows with the text, max 4 lines. Position: x 568, y 1100 in the 2:3 frame; x 572, y 1292 in the 9:16 frame. The four ruled lines in the 2:3 frame are at y 1149, 1213, 1277 and 1342.
Shrink rule: if the message needs more than 4 lines at 42px, reduce the font size, down to a minimum of 34px. If it still doesn't fit, use the shorter fallback.
Build bg_texture and card_art as image assets exported from Figma at 1x of the frame size (1080 wide) or higher.

notes: The user picks any photo; the message is prefilled with the same rules and can be edited.

followUps: None. The old tiger stamp has been replaced by the "MEMORY" suitcase stamp as its own layer.
